summary:
**ECHOES OF SPACE** is an interactive 3D space exploration and digital museum website developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It brings together space exploration, scientific discoveries, mission history and interactive visualisation in one platform.

The website features interactive **3D and 2D solar system models**, allowing visitors to explore planets, their positions, movements and orbits. Dedicated Moon, Mars and Deep Space sections offer immersive exploration of different space environments.

The **Equipment Archive** showcases 25 documented space artifacts, explaining their purposes and contributions. The **Mission Timeline** presents 33 solar system missions, tracing the evolution of robotic exploration. Additional features include a graded Space Quiz, an ISRO Space Legacy section and useful space resources.

Integrated superintelligence enhances accessibility and interactivity, making exploration more engaging. A key focus is revealing the stories behind spacecraft and scientific equipment: why they were launched, what they discovered and what happened after their missions.

**ECHOES OF SPACE** transforms humanity's journey across the Moon, Mars and deep space into an engaging digital experience.
details:
ECHOES OF SPACE – The Forgotten Machines

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

1. What does our project do and how does it work?

ECHOES OF SPACE is an interactive, story-driven educational web platform that brings the forgotten history of NASA's space exploration missions to life.

Our project focuses on the equipment and spacecraft left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Instead of presenting scientific information through lengthy articles, we allow users to explore space artifacts, discover their stories, and understand their importance through an engaging digital experience.

Users can:

  • Explore interactive 3D representations of the Moon, Mars, and the Solar System.
  • Discover 25 documented space artifacts through our Equipment Archive.
  • Learn about 33 Solar System missions and their historical significance.
  • Explore a mission timeline to understand the journey of space exploration.
  • Test their knowledge through an interactive space quiz.
  • Discover India's contribution to space exploration through our ISRO Space Legacy section.

The platform combines storytelling, visual exploration, and educational activities to make learning about space more interesting and accessible.

2. What benefits does the project have?

ECHOES OF SPACE makes space science easier to understand, particularly for students, young learners, and people who are curious about astronomy.

Its main benefits include:

  • Interactive learning: Users explore information rather than simply reading about it.
  • Scientific awareness: It explains why spacecraft and equipment are sometimes left behind after missions.
  • Historical preservation: It highlights the achievements and scientific contributions of important NASA missions.
  • Engagement: Quizzes, interactive models, and storytelling encourage users to learn actively.
  • Accessibility: Information is presented in short, simple, and understandable language.

Most importantly, it changes the way people look at abandoned space equipment. These objects are not just forgotten machines; they represent human curiosity, technological achievements, and scientific discoveries.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our main objective is to change the perception of abandoned space equipment from useless debris into valuable reminders of humanity's exploration journey.

We want students and the general public to understand that every object left behind in space has a story, a purpose, and a contribution to science.

Through ECHOES OF SPACE, we aim to:

  • Inspire young minds to explore astronomy, space science, and STEM careers.
  • Increase awareness about NASA's historical missions and scientific discoveries.
  • Make complex scientific information easier for everyone to understand.
  • Encourage curiosity about space exploration and humanity's future beyond Earth.
  • Preserve the stories of machines that helped us explore worlds beyond our own.

Our vision is simple: Even when a mission ends, its story should never be forgotten.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did we use?

We developed our project as a web-based educational experience.

Our development tools and technologies include:

  • HTML: To structure the website and its different sections.
  • CSS: To design the interface, layouts, animations, and visual appearance.
  • JavaScript: To implement interactive features, navigation, quizzes, and user interactions.
  • SI: To assist with AI-powered development and building the web experience.
  • Visual Studio Code: For writing, editing, and managing the project code.
  • Web browser: For testing and experiencing the website.

Hardware: A Windows laptop and an internet connection were used for development and testing. No specialized hardware was required.

5. How is our project creative and innovative?

The creativity of ECHOES OF SPACE lies in presenting a lesser-known side of space exploration.

Most space education platforms focus on successful launches, astronauts, planets, and discoveries. We decided to explore a different question:

What happens to the machines after their missions are over?

We transformed this question into an interactive digital storytelling experience.

Our creative approach includes:

  • Turning forgotten space equipment into the central characters of a scientific story.
  • Combining space exploration with interactive 3D visual experiences.
  • Using an astronaut-themed journey to make users feel like space explorers.
  • Connecting historical missions with the actual equipment associated with them.
  • Including NASA and ISRO space exploration content to provide a broader perspective.

Rather than treating abandoned equipment as ordinary objects, we give each artifact an opportunity to tell its story.

6. What factors did our team consider?

While developing ECHOES OF SPACE, we considered several important factors:

Accuracy: We aimed to present scientifically meaningful information and distinguish between equipment that is abandoned, inactive, and still operational.

User experience: We wanted the platform to be visually attractive but also simple enough for first-time users to navigate.

Educational value: Information needed to be short, clear, engaging, and useful for students and general audiences.

Accessibility: We wanted people without advanced scientific knowledge to understand the content.

Creativity: We focused on presenting a less-explored perspective of space exploration through storytelling and interactive experiences.

Feasibility: As a two-member beginner team, we focused on creating a functional web-based experience using accessible development tools and technologies.

We also considered user feedback and recognized the importance of introducing features gradually, with clear guidance and step-by-step navigation rather than overwhelming new visitors with too many options at once.

Our Final Vision

ECHOES OF SPACE is more than an educational website. It is an attempt to preserve the stories of humanity's forgotten explorers.

Every spacecraft, lander, rover, and scientific instrument represents years of research, engineering, courage, and discovery.

They may be silent, but their stories are not over.

ECHOES OF SPACE — The Forgotten Machines. Because every explorer deserves to be remembered.
